openings.claim: Sideways retention may use padded hatch-edge bearing independently of downward seal compression, allowing lift-out reopening.
openings.delta: Replace tighter left-corner pressing with two removable rim-only guides assembled from the four strips and supplied bolts. Pads protect contact surfaces; guide faces locate hatch edges without increasing seal compression. Drill or cut only supplied strips. Use cord to retain removed parts outside the full inspection opening. Exact guide geometry remains unproved.
openings.prediction: Compared with the nearest rival, tighter left-corner pressing, guides should withstand 20 N with displacement at most 1 mm without reproducing the stipulated 2 mm opposite-corner lift. After ten openings, the final closure with the right-contact 1 mm card should meet position, pull, reopening-time and seal-tear requirements; only seal contact continuity is exempt. Rival failure is not assumed.
openings.probe: Before counting trials, inspect rim access, hatch-edge engagement, bolt reach, pad placement and lift-out clearance with ruler and supplied parts. Proceed only if a reversible assembly can carry lateral force without forbidden alteration. Allocate two closure/pull trials to pressing, one disturbed, then ten to guides, each following an opening cycle and with the final closure disturbed: twelve total. Mark hatch position; measure pull displacement, opposite-corner lift and each reopening time with scale, ruler and stopwatch. Inspect seal after each cycle. Record assembly feasibility and whether fabrication and observations fit ninety and twenty minutes respectively. An infeasible assembly yields no performance comparison.
assumptions: Rim cross-section, bolt lengths, achievable guide clearance, pad compression and strip capacity are indispensable unknowns; listed resources do not establish feasibility.

Defeat includes guide slip, clearance exceeding position tolerance, dependence on extra seal compression, forbidden alteration, obstruction, unrecoverable parts, seal damage, any outcome failure, or exhausted time/material capacity.
Success supports only this fixture, load and disturbance. Separating load paths is a hypothesis, not reliable performance or deployment authorization.

assessment: One uncertain opening. Geometry verification enables the comparison; a trial cap alone cannot establish an informative feasible test.

lineage.reason: Preserve separated lateral bearing; specify feasibility checks, ten opening cycles, measurements and twelve-trial allocation without inventing geometry or results.
